method: Original deterministic code-native SVG connected panel layout; original physical groups retained, vertical positions and minimum font sizes adjusted

exactOriginalMemberTasksAndGuards.task: Apply breast-and-node invasive clearance versus a stricter no-in-situ definition to the same component findings.
exactOriginalMemberTasksAndGuards.gap: The checklist framing is sound, but the two definitions and changed nodal fact require a three-component contrast. A small breast-invasive/breast-in-situ/nodal table-diagram could make the permitted DCIS difference explicit; no cure stamp or whole-body illustration is appropriate.
guardrails: Defined complete-surgical assessment, not negative scan/blood/small biopsy.
Residual DCIS can meet the common definition but remains a finding.
Do not infer cure, clear margins or trial-level survival benefit.

sourceDepth: Same existing selected CAP/FDA/NCI/CONSORT passages and archived primary abstracts; no new access/science/clinical claim

readerCopy.title: Apply both response definitions
readerCopy.alt: Panel 2 of 2. The same fictional post-treatment cases share no residual invasive breast cancer, residual DCIS and identical DCIS at final ink. Case A has no residual nodal cancer found; case B has a fictional 4 mm invasive nodal deposit. A meets ypT0/Tis ypN0 but not ypT0 ypN0; B meets neither. Response does not settle margins or mean cure. Panel 1 shows the breast and nodal components.
readerCopy.caption: Panel 2 of 2: case A meets ypT0/Tis ypN0 but not ypT0 ypN0; case B meets neither. The identical ink findings remain a separate margin question.

acceptedOverallCaption: Keep the definition beside the component findings. Permitted DCIS can coexist with a margin question, and residual invasive nodal disease changes the combined endpoint.
